abstract.t:
XCIM specifies evidence that a party controlling an email address explicitly consented to receive defined types of communication from an identified sender. A trusted third-party Consent Attester verifies address control, observes a separate affirmative decision, and signs an attestation binding the recipient, sender, and agreed types. Blockchain anchoring provides immutable evidence of the attestation under an admitted finality policy. Authenticated lifecycle events and fresh status distinguish the historical decision from current consent.
XCIM concerns the consent relationship independently of individual email messages. It does not sign, inspect, classify, or authenticate their content. A receiving email service may use verified current consent as a positive policy signal after independently establishing the sender identity relevant to its query. This document defines a portable consent object format and verification contract, together with requirements for separately admitted blockchain adapters. It does not select a universal blockchain network or claim operational readiness.
